traits.label: Hymenium
traits.text: Initially solid, becoming powdery with maturity due to the transformation of the internal tissue into spores.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium: Initially solid, becoming powdery with maturity due to the transformation of the internal tissue into spores.

traits.label: Fruit body
traits.text: Globose to slightly pear-shaped puffball, smooth to finely granulated or spiny at a young age; spines, if present, often fall off with age, leaving a net-like pattern.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Fruit body: Globose to slightly pear-shaped puffball, smooth to finely granulated or spiny at a young age; spines, if present, often fall off with age, leaving a net-like pattern.

traits.label: Color
traits.text: Dark brown to olive-brown when mature.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Color: Dark brown to olive-brown when mature.

traits.label: Ecology
traits.text: Grasslands, meadows, and forest clearings; often found growing in groups.
traits.raw: 🌱 Grasslands, meadows, and forest clearings; often found growing in groups.

traits.label: Edibility
traits.text: Edible when young and the internal flesh is white and firm, but not considered a top choice.
traits.raw: 🙂 Edible when young and the internal flesh is white and firm, but not considered a top choice.

traits.label: Fruit body
traits.text: Fruit body: Up to 2-4 cm in diameter.
traits.raw: 📏 Fruit body: Up to 2-4 cm in diameter.

traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Distinguished by its small size and dark, umber to olive-brown coloration at maturity. Young specimens can be consumed when the inner flesh is still white and hasn't transformed into spores. With age, pressing on the mature puffball will release a brown "smoke" of spores.
traits.raw: 🔤 Distinguished by its small size and dark, umber to olive-brown coloration at maturity. Young specimens can be consumed when the inner flesh is still white and hasn't transformed into spores. With age, pressing on the mature puffball will release a brown "smoke" of spores.
